glossary.Haematoma: A collection of clotted blood outside a blood vessel.
glossary.Temporal bone fracture: A break in the skull bone at the side of the head, just above the ear.
glossary.Temple: The flat area at the side of the head between the eye and the ear, where the skull is thin.
glossary.Raised ICP: Raised intracranial pressure: pressure inside the skull rises, causing headache, vomiting and falling consciousness.
glossary.Focal signs: Neurological signs pointing to damage in one specific part of the brain, such as one-sided weakness.
glossary.Fixed dilated pupil: A large pupil that does not constrict to light, a sign of third nerve compression.
glossary.Brainstem: The base of the brain (midbrain, pons, medulla) controlling breathing, heart rate and consciousness.
glossary.Brainstem compression: Squashing of the brainstem by a swelling brain, threatening breathing and heart control.
glossary.Irregular respirations: Abnormal, uneven breathing pattern from brainstem compression.
glossary.Seizures: Fits: bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
glossary.Neurological deficit: Loss of a nerve or brain function, such as weakness, numbness or speech loss.
glossary.Neurosurgical emergency: A condition needing urgent brain surgery to prevent death or disability.
glossary.Neurosurgery: The surgical specialty that operates on the brain, spine and nerves.
glossary.Haematoma evacuation: Surgically removing a collection of blood to relieve pressure on the brain.
glossary.Evacuation: Surgical removal of a collection, such as a blood clot.
glossary.Decompression: Relieving pressure, here by opening the skull to let out blood.
glossary.Parasympathetic fibres: Nerve fibres running on the outside of CN III that constrict the pupil; squashed first, so the pupil dilates.
glossary.Laceration: A tear or cut in tissue.
glossary.Loss of consciousness: Being unresponsive and unaware of surroundings.
glossary.Reduced consciousness: Drowsiness or unresponsiveness, measured with the GCS.
glossary.Arterial bleed: Bleeding from an artery: high pressure, so it collects quickly.
glossary.Extradural: Outside the dura: between the skull and the dura mater.
glossary.Skull: The bony case around the brain.
glossary.Critical volume: The point where the brain can no longer compensate for added volume and ICP shoots up.
glossary.Neurological deterioration: Worsening brain function: falling GCS, new weakness or pupil changes.
